items.followUp: Define the proportional limit of a material.

rubric.why: Checks that the elastic limit is identified as the greatest or maximum force or stress up to which elastic recovery occurs.
rubric.description: States that the elastic limit is the greatest or maximum deforming force or stress.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the limiting maximum force or stress.

rubric.why: Checks the defining recovery condition after removal of the force.
rubric.description: States that the body regains its original shape and size when the force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both the recovery and force-removal condition.

modelAnswer: The elastic limit is the greatest value of deforming force up to which a body regains its original shape and size when the force is removed.

items.followUp: A vehicle increases its velocity from 5 m s⁻¹ to 25 m s⁻¹ in 10 s. Find its acceleration.

rubric.why: Checks that the initial velocity, final velocity and time are correctly identified.
rubric.description: Writes the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying u = 0 m s⁻¹, v = 20 m s⁻¹ and t = 8 s.

rubric.why: Checks use of the acceleration relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct acceleration formula.

rubric.why: Checks correct substitution of the given values into the formula.
Checks the numerical evaluation of the acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical value.

rubric.why: Checks that acceleration is expressed in the correct SI unit.
rubric.description: Gives the answer in m s⁻².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct acceleration unit.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 0 m s⁻¹, v = 20 m s⁻¹, t = 8 s.
Substitution: a = (20 m s⁻¹ − 0 m s⁻¹)/8 s.
Calculation: a = 20/8 m s⁻² = 2.5 m s⁻².
Answer: The acceleration of the car is 2.5 m s⁻².

items.followUp: Derive the equation for gravitational potential energy near Earth’s surface.

rubric.why: Checks the defining link between kinetic energy and a body's motion.
rubric.description: Defines kinetic energy as the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Checks that the derivation starts from work done and Newton’s second law.
rubric.description: Uses W = Fs and F = ma.

rubric.why: Checks the kinematic relation and the resulting displacement for a body starting from rest.
rubric.description: Uses the kinematic equation to obtain s = v²/(2a).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct kinematic step and displacement expression.

rubric.why: Checks that the work expression is reduced to the kinetic-energy equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the derived kinetic-energy equation.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
For a body starting from rest, v² − u² = 2as and u = 0.
Since F = ma, W = Fs = ma × v²/(2a).
Thus, kinetic energy, K.E. = W = ½mv².
